title: Polo-like-kinase-2-dependent α-Synuclein Serine-129 Phosphorylation: a Physiological RoleDuring Synaptic Activity
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on the synaptic biology of α-synu-
clein, the central protein in the pathogenesis of Parkinson’s disease and other devastating brain diseases, in-
cluding dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer’s disease. Unexpected findings by the applicants demonstrate
that α-synuclein serine-129 phosphorylation, a protein modification commonly associated with pathology, occurs
normally during synaptic activity with major implications for developing treatments for synuclein diseases and
establishing signatures of their early and advanced progression. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to
NINDS’s mission of seeking fundamental knowledge about the brain and nervous system and to use that
knowledge to reduce the burden of neurological disease, i.e., Parkinson’s disease, Dementia with Lewy bodies
and Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Targeting PFC interneurons for personalized treatments in OUD
text:
New treatments are desperately needed for the persistent symptoms of opioid use disorder (OUD), including
changes in mood, motivation, and cravings. This proposal is designed to improve our understanding of how
discrete aspects of prefrontal cortex neural circuit function are related to behavioral changes following long-
term fentanyl self-administration. Our goal is to develop translational metrics that will guide the development
and utility of next-generation treatments for OUD.

title: Multi-modality detection of RCC Recurrence Post Ablation
text:
Localized ablation is a recommended treatment for T1a renal cancers and increasingly used as a non-surgical
treatment option. Detection of cancer recurrence by CT or MRI (the current clinical standard) can be problematic
due to patient contraindications, low temporal resolution, and cost. We propose multi-modality contrast-
enhanced ultrasound to detect recurrent renal cancer following ablation and propose to compare its performance
to contrast-enhanced cross-sectional imaging in a fully powered clinical study.

title: Decoding global RNP topologies in splicing regulation
text:
Alternative splicing is a major mechanism that generates the diverse proteome during development and is
frequently disrupted in many human diseases. We develop a new technology, SHARCLIP, to build a
transcriptome-wide structure-interaction map for pre-mRNP complexes on which alternative splicing occurs.
This technology and resource will help understand mechanisms of splicing-related diseases and empower
future RNA-targeting therapeutics.

title: Genetic analysis of signaling pathways in cilia assembly and remodeling
text: Primary cilia concentrate molecular machinery of all major signaling pathways thus allowing cells to communicate with their environment, and cilia defects cause a spectrum of disorders called ciliopathies. The proposed research is relevant to public health because it aims to identify new genes and map pathways in cilia assembly and post-developmental remodeling. This fundamental knowledge has the potential to facilitate development of therapeutic strategies to manage human conditions caused by anatomical and functional cilia abnormalities

title: Unlocking Pediatric Genomic Variation: A Proposal to Index and Genotype the Kids First Cohort with The Great Genotyper
text:
This project will create the first graph-based genomic index of over 30,000 children’s whole genomes
from the Kids First program, enabling real-time analysis of structural variants linked to congenital and pediatric
diseases. Researchers will gain secure, web-based access to allele frequencies and genotypes across the
cohort without reanalyzing raw data. The resulting resource will accelerate the identification of pathogenic
structural variants, and advance precision medicine for children affected by rare developmental and cancer-
related disorders.

title: Epitope-engineered HSCs to permit CAR-T cell-mediated CD4-depletion for HIV cure
text:
This work introduces an HIV cure strategy that combines autologous HSCT, precise CD4-targeted base editing,
and CAR T cell therapy to protect newly generated immune cells while eliminating residual HIV reservoirs. By
overcoming CCR5-independent variants, reservoir persistence, and the risks of allogeneic transplantation, this
approach has the potential to enable durable HIV remission in otherwise healthy people living with HIV.

title: Montefiore Einstein Clinical Oncology Training Program in the Bronx
text:
The objective of this program is to train clinical and translational physician-scientists to develop new cancer
treatments and improve cancer care delivery at the Montefiore Einstein cancer center. This will be achieved
through a coordinated program of mentoring, innovative didactic courses, and emphasis on 
care delivery for environmentally exposed population via an interdisciplinary collaborative design.

title: Exploring the Subthalamic Nucleus Role in Variability Regulation
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Obsessive compulsive disorder, autism spectrum disorders or substance use disorder affect the neuronal
circuitry that regulates behavioral variability. Our research aims to understand these circuits, focusing on a novel,
variability-promoting pathway in the basal ganglia. Our insights will help to explain pathological deficits in the
various disorders causing invariable behaviors and may aid the development of tailored therapeutics in the
future.

title: Stressful life events confer risk for chronic posttraumatic musculoskeletal pain through DNA methylation changes at the POMC promoter
text:
Chronic pain is common, highly morbid, and extremely costly to society; interventions that reduce
chronic pain are limited. A lack of effective treatments is partially due to an incomplete understanding
of molecular mechanisms driving chronic pain development. The training award proposes to use
translational research methods to test hypotheses focused on how DNA methylation levels contribute
to biopsychosocial mechanisms leading to chronic post-traumatic pain development.

title: Ghana IntegRative Approach to Cancer ResEarch Training: The Grace Program
text:
Page 7
Cancer incidence is significantly increasing in the United States, partly due to an aging population, as well as in sub-Saharan African countries such as Ghana, necessitating a shift in training and research to address this growing problem in a way that mutually benefits the cancer research efforts in the US and Ghana. Expansive genetic diversity and high burden of advanced disease in Ghana provides limitless potential for researchers to contribute to greater understanding of cancer risk stratification and treatment of aggressive and metastatic cancer in US cancer patients of African ancestry – research that cannot be done with US populations alone. A collaborative multinational cancer research training program joining institutions from the US and Ghana increases capacity for international collaborations that cultivate unique opportunities for the reciprocal exchange of knowledge, skills, and innovative training approaches to address the increasing burden of cancer globally. As such, we propose a 5-year cancer research training program titled, the “Ghana integRative Approach to Cancer rEsearch: The GRACE Program,” to strengthen existing partnerships between Moffitt Cancer Center and the Ghana Health Systems (e.g., University of Ghana Medical School, Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, College of Physicians and Surgeons) by augmenting educational materials that provide, short-, medium, and sustained long-term cross-institutional cancer research training that can be adapted for US settings that include similar underserved communities across the US and Ghana like rural and low-income.

title: Pre-Doctoral Pharmacology Training Program
text:
The Pre-Doctoral Pharmacology Training Program (PPTP) at Yale University will provide rigorous, advanced
training in the pharmacological sciences by employing innovative teaching methodologies and cutting-edge
technologies. The PPTP will prepare students for research and research-related careers in academia, industry,
and the non-profit sector.

title: Identification of small molecule activators of Type I interferon signaling for cancer treatment
text:
In recent years, immunotherapies have revolutionized cancer treatment by leveraging the body's
immune system, however, many patients remain refractory to this potential cure. One attractive
option to enhance immunotherapy is to activate the interferon (IFN) receptor and downstream
pathways, but a negative feedback mechanism mediated by a key regulator called USP18 has
thus far limited this approach. Our objective is to identify a first-in-class drug that can disrupt this
feedback loop and release the full potential of IFN to enhance the body's immune response
against cancer leading to more effective therapies.

title: Digital Accessible Remote Olfactory Mediated Health Assessments forPreclinical AD
text: Detecting clinically normal individuals over 55 years old with Alzheimer’s disease pathology and following their disease progression in a non-invasive, affordable manner is a critical step to developing and monitoring disease-modifying therapies. We developed the AROMHA Brain Health Test, a web-based app to identify cognitively healthy elderly individuals at risk for progression to MCI. To seek further validation of this promising methodology, we propose to examine its utility in participants in three geographically distinct AD Research Centers with relevant populations and in real-world settings, mobile medical units in Chicago and in 55+ communities.

title: Stem Cell Dysfunction in Aged Skeletal Muscle
text:
One of the biggest medical issues affecting the elderly population is the progressive loss of muscle
mass and strength. Recently, we discovered a new FOS/NAD/ART1-MARylation adult stem cell
activation pathway that stimulates skeletal muscle repair after injury. In this project, we will explore
whether this understudied pathway is disrupted in aged skeletal muscle, and whether restoring its
levels can reverse the muscle dysfunction associated with the ageing process.

title: Determining the factors that impact single stranded DNA mutagenesis
text:
Single stranded DNA has been demonstrated to be hypermutable by a variety of environmental and
endogenous mutagens. However, the factors that modulate the susceptibility and specificity of mutagens to
ssDNA are not well known. This proposal will investigate genetic factors that impact the mutagenesis of ssDNA
in yeast and in cancers.

title: Employing viruses to unravel the functional significance of the m5C epitranscriptome
text: 5-methylcytosine (m5C) is an understudied but important RNA modification, often dysregulated in developmental disorders, cancer and more. We propose a comprehensive study exploiting RNA viruses whose genomes are m5C methylated to understand the role of m5C in regulating RNA biology, including the activities responsible for adding and recognizing this modification. In addition to significantly advancing the m5C field, this work will also contribute to the development of antiviral strategies against viruses causing significant human disease such as chikungunya virus and Coxsackie virus.

title: (3 of 3) MMC, VICC & TSU: Partners in Eliminating Cancer Disparities
text:
The Meharry /Vanderbilt-Tennessee State Cancer Partnership (MVTCP) aligns with NIH priorities
by addressing persistent cancer disparities by supporting collaborative research, training, and
community engagement across two Resource Limited Institutions (RLI) and an NCI-designated
cancer center. This administrative supplement will maintain critical operational infrastructure and
core research support needed to sustain ongoing partnership activities. By preserving essential
partnership functions, funding will ensure the partnership can quickly respond to the notice of
funding opportunity once issued and enable ongoing progress toward improving cancer outcomes
for all.

title: Engineering photostable fluorescent proteins and biosensors using transcriptomic mining and massive-throughput single-cell screening
text:
Fluorescent proteins are broadly used reporters of gene expression, protein localization, and cellular activity in
health and disease. However, the brightness of fluorescent proteins and biosensors decreases with prolonged
illumination, limiting their utility for long-term imaging. The authors of this proposal propose extending the
duration of biological imaging by developing fluorescent proteins and biosensors with improved photostability.

title: Identifying Plasmodium Liver-Stage Secreted Effector Proteins
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because, a mechanistic understanding of how
malaria parasites evade immune responses generated in the liver is expected to promote the
development of new anti-malarial drugs. This research is therefore relevant to the core mission
of the NIH pertaining to acquisition of fundamental knowledge about the nature and behavior of
living systems, and the application of that knowledge to enhance health, and reduce the burdens
of illness in our society.
